title: lean gemmini + low-level ISA problem
body:
I'm synthesizing and simulating gemmini with firesim. And I get the same error when testing some hardware.

Default gemmini gave no errors, but when gemmini is set to lean gemmini, the simulation never ends when running ResNet-50 with low-level ISA.

I didn't include the assert option in firesim platform config, so I'm not sure exactly why it never end.

But I got some logs by including firesim print option and perfcount option, and those logs are blow.

fix_commits.messageHeadline: Fix Unpredictable Infinite Stall Caused By OS Interrupts (#189)

comments.body: Additionally, if the same hardware and the same binary(low-level ISA) are simulated on the midas verilator platform, it seems to work without any problem.

I'm building the `leanConfig` in FireSim now to try to reproduce this.

Just so I'm clear, are these the steps you followed?
* Build the `leanConfig` in Firesim
* Run `resnet50-linux` on the `leanConfig` in FireSim
* Observe that `resnet50-linux` never finishes, and never prints anything

> Build the leanConfig in Firesim
> Run resnet50-linux on the leanConfig in FireSim
> Observe that resnet50-linux never finishes, and never prints anything

Yes, I followed these the steps.

Additionally, I builded and tested various `leanConfig` Gemmini with different CPU and L2 cache.

```
class LeanGemminiRocketConfig extends Config(
  new gemmini.DefaultGemminiConfig(gemmini.GemminiConfigs.leanConfig) ++
  new freechips.rocketchip.subsystem.WithNBigCores(1) ++
  new chipyard.config.AbstractConfig)

class LeanGemmini2MBRocketConfig extends Config(
  new gemmini.DefaultGemminiConfig(gemmini.GemminiConfigs.leanConfig) ++
  new freechips.rocketchip.subsystem.WithNBigCores(1) ++
  new freechips.rocketchip.subsystem.WithInclusiveCache(capacityKB=2048) ++
  new chipyard.config.AbstractConfig)

class LeanGemminiLargeBoomConfig extends Config(
  new gemmini.DefaultGemminiConfig(gemmini.GemminiConfigs.leanConfig) ++
  new boom.common.WithNLargeBooms(1) ++
  new chipyard.config.AbstractConfig)
```

I also tested this hardware with various `resnet50-linux` configured as low level ISA but using different double buffer options and printing the current I, J, K tile numbers.

and the results are below.

| hardware                   | loop ISA | low-level ISA | low-level ISA w/ print IJK | low-level ISA w/ double buffer |
|----------------------------|----------|---------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------|
| leanConf + Rocket          |     o    |       x       |              o             |                 x                |
| leanConf + Boom            |     o    |       x       |              x             |                 x                |
| leanConf + Rocket + 2MB L2 |     o    |       x       |              x             |                 x                |

Sorry, can you explain what the difference is between your `loop ISA` tests and `low-level ISA` tests?

Did you change `gemmini.h` to run the `low-level ISA` tests?

Could you share a copy of your "low-level ISA `gemmini.h`". You could save it in a [Gist](https://gist.github.com/).

I think I know what changes you made, but I just want to be sure I'm running the same thing

This is my gemmini.h https://gist.github.com/thuako/ff419c06ce3eaa5e8292532d307cdca4

Thank you for your interest in this issue.
I'm able to replicate this issue. I'll try to figure out the cause of this bug, though this won't be very high-priority, since the loop-ISA seems to be working fine.

I started developing on top of gemmini to create NPUs for specific workloads because gemmini is the most versatile and compatible when comparing other NPU platforms.

But the NPU I made seems to have the same bugs as leanConfig , even though I haven't changed max flight requests. (There is no bug on midas platform, but on firesim it is stopped by gemmini_timeout assert. And if I put printf between the loops, it works fine.)

In the end, I'm making LoopMatmul and LoopConv dedicated to specific workloads to solve the CPU bottleneck and the bug above.

However, as #161 , loop-ISA has some drawbacks in terms of versatility.

So, even if this issue isn't a high priority right now, I think this problem should be resolved for many people to use Gemmini.

Thanks for your response!

Quick update:

I'm still debugging this. The error seems to be caused by a `preload` instruction which is issued from the `ReservationStation` to the `ExecuteController`, but is never marked as "complete" by the `ExecuteController`.

This seems to be very timing-dependent, which means I haven't been able to replicate this on VCS or MIDAS. Debugging on FireSim is a lot slower than debugging on VCS/MIDAS, but I'm still making progress.

Thank you for giving me updates.

And I have a one question. Is it common for bugs to occur only in firesim?

Not very common.

In this case, I believe the bug is occurring because OS interrupts are exposing a bug in the ReservationStation.

With Verilator/MIDAS, we're not running Linux, so these interrupts don't happen.

This bug should have been fixed by https://github.com/ucb-bar/gemmini/pull/189, which has been merged into the `dev` branch.

I'm closing this issue for now, but if you find that it still persists even on the `dev` branch, then feel free to re-open it.
